study_id: Ayers et al. - 2021 - Using machine learning to improve survival prediction after heart transplantation

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study is a peer‑reviewed 2021 observational analysis of adult heart transplant recipients using ensemble machine learning (non‑linear) to predict 1‑year survival, meeting all population, intervention, comparator, outcome, and study design criteria.

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective study using UNOS registry to predict 1-year survival after heart transplantation with machine learning ensemble models.
identification_methods.Institution: Department of Surgery, The Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, Massachusetts, USA
identification_methods.Address: 30 Courtenay Dr, MSC 295, Suite BM279, Charleston, SC 29425, USA
identification_methods.Dataset Source: United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) registry
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult patients undergoing primary, isolated orthotopic heart transplantation between 2000 and 2019; excluded patients <18 years, prior transplant, multiorgan transplant, or incomplete 1‑year survival data.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Ensemble of deep neural network, logistic regression, AdaBoost, and random forest (400 algorithms total)
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Over‑sampling with SVM SMOTE and under‑sampling with Repeated Edited Nearest Neighbors
identification_methods.Comparator: Singular logistic regression and individual algorithm models
identification_methods.Input Variables: 47 preoperative variables selected from UNOS after manual and automated feature selection (demographics, labs, donor/recipient characteristics)
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Variables with >20% missing excluded; continuous variables imputed with median, categorical with mode
identification_methods.Validation Method: Random split into 80% training and 20% validation cohorts; internal validation on held‑out set
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Feature importance via univariate random forest; dimensionality reduction; ensemble modeling of 400 algorithms; calibration plots; performance assessed with AUROC, NRI, and decision curve analysis

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult patients undergoing primary, isolated orthotopic heart transplantation (OHT) between 2000 and 2019
population.Exclusion criteria: Patients <18 years, prior heart transplantation, multiorgan transplant, incomplete 1‑year survival status
population.Population Notes: Patients randomly split into training (80%) and validation (20%) cohorts

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: Ensemble model combining deep neural network, logistic regression, AdaBoost, and random forest
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Preoperative clinical variables from UNOS registry
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: Manual review plus univariate random forest importance, top features combined
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Oversampling (SMOTE) and undersampling applied; 400 algorithms trained and combined into final ensemble
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Ensemble model achieved AUROC 0.764 (95% CI 0.745–0.782), p<0.001, NRI improvement 72.9%±3.8%
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All orthotopic heart transplant recipients in validation cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Ensemble model outperformed individual models and logistic regression
